deploy-bot: [AUTO] Canary deploy paused: release 2026.03.21-eu — detected 5xx spike from redis-eu. Holding downstream windows and any scheduled rollouts.
ops-oncall: On it, pulling metrics and checking redis cluster health.
alex: Can we pin traffic to the previous stable (2026.03.14-eu) while we investigate? :thinking:
maria: Agree with pin. No DB migrations in this release, so pin / reroute should be low risk.
sam: Confirmed: release contains only model config + frontend toggle, safe to pin.
jordan: I'll update the release calendar and shift dependent releases by +2h for now.
lee: If we need to, we can rollback canary hosts only: `deployctl rollback --hosts eu-canary --to 2026.03.14-eu`
ops-oncall: Running pre-rollback checks. If latency/5xx normalizes within 15m we try resume with traffic cap. Otherwise we'll rollback canary.
alex: I'll add a short note to the release notes: "Incident-triggered hold — pinned to previous stable until verification."
maria: Also create a postmortem placeholder and link to the incident channel (inc-2026-0316).
deploy-bot: Resume blocked until ops sign-off. Admins: use `@deploy-bot force-resume` only with explicit approval.
ops-oncall: 1729004441: metrics look stable, redis node errors cleared. Recommend resuming canary at 10% traffic cap and watch for 10m.
jordan: Reschedule window: moved to +10:00 UTC to allow staging smoke tests. Requeued affected releases in the Console (note: manual approval required).
alex: Pin + requeue done. I'll follow up with a brief in #postmortems and update the runbook section about incident-driven holds.
maria: Thanks — will coordinate the canary verification and unpin if green. :thumbsup:
